newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil must stop using inflation excuse - Dornbusch.
newsitem.headline: Brazil must stop using inflation excuse - Dornbusch.

text.p: Brazil must move on and stop using the battle against inflation as an excuse for slow economic growth, said economist Rudiger Dornbusch in a interview with weekly Brazilian magazine Veja published Saturday.

"Inflation continues to be used as the main excuse for why Brazil is not modernising itself, not making fiscal and administrative reforms and is not growing again," said Dornbusch, an economics professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).

"Before the Brazilian authorities said the country was dominated by monstrously high inflation and because of this not a lot could be done. Now they are saying Brazil needs to maintain low inflation and this does not leave time or the energy to promote grouth," he added.
Dornbusch in June this year raised questions at the International Monetary Conference regarding Brazil's economy and the heavy capital flows into the country.

In the Veja article, Dornbusch praised the country's anti- inflationary Real Plan "not because it contains good and tested economics as we known them," but because it has succeeded in "defeating inflation without fiscal austerity".
However, one cost of lower inflation has been the pruning of the Brazilian banking system which has still not stabilised, he said.

"It will come out saying that I am predicting a collapse in the Brazilian banking system, but the truth is that with current interest rates in Brazil, there is no bank that can manage to survive for very long," Dornbusch said.
Dornbusch reiterated that he was not predicting imminent disaster.

"I think there is always time to correct mistakes. If people still accept my advice in Brazil, here are some suggestions -- stay calm, do not sacrifice the educational system in the name of the blind fight against inflation, do not kill the banking system, do not remove the possibility of growth nor the competitive sector of the market," he said.
Dornbusch gave his views on other topics:
RE-ELECTION
"I support Fernando Henrique Cardoso being given another mandate. This would help to create a favorable environment for the development of the economy."
FOREIGN CAPITAL INFLOWS

"Attracting capital is not a measure for the health of an economy. Money is going into Brazil because of extraordinary interest rates. Let's not interpret this as a signal of foreign confidence in Brazil."
FOREIGN INVESTMENT
"(Direct investment) coming into Brazil is very little in comparison with what other countries are attracting....What is going to Brazil are leftovers."
REFORMS
"What exasperates me is that Brazil has no excuse for skating around reforms. If this was Argentina, a broken country full of crises, perhaps it would be justified. Brazil has no excuse".
STABILISATION OF THE REAL

"The stabilisation of the currency was done brilliantly, but life goes on. A country like Brazil with two years of economic stability should have already turned the record over and started to revolutionise the educational system and mechanisms to form a work force. There is no future in the world today for a country that does not give priority to education, that does not have innovative ideas on how to train its massive working population".
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
